command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Solving algebraic and modulus inequalities
kcs.statement: The manipulation and solution of algebraic inequalities and inequations, including those involving the modulus sign.
kcs.raw: The manipulation and solution of algebraic inequalities and inequations, including those involving the modulus sign.
kcs.guidance: The solution of inequalities such as $\dfrac{1}{x} > x$, $|x^2 - 1| > 2(x+1)$ and $\dfrac{1}{x-a} > \dfrac{1}{x-b}$.

kcs.title: Method of differences for series
kcs.statement: Summation of simple finite series using the method of differences.
kcs.raw: Summation of simple finite series using the method of differences.
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to sum series such as $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} \dfrac{1}{r(r+1)}$ using partial fractions such as $\dfrac{1}{r(r+1)} = \dfrac{1}{r} - \dfrac{1}{r+1}$.

kcs.title: Euler's relation for complex exponentials
kcs.raw: Euler’s relation eiθ = cos θ + i sin θ.
kcs.guidance: Students should be familiar with $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}(e^{i\theta} + e^{-i\theta})$ and $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2i}(e^{i\theta} - e^{-i\theta})$.

kcs.title: De Moivre's theorem and applications
kcs.statement: De Moivre's theorem and its application to trigonometric identities and to roots of a complex number.
kcs.raw: De Moivre’s theorem and its application to trigonometric identities and to roots of a complex number.
glossary: nth roots of a complex number
kcs.guidance: To include finding $\cos n\theta$ and $\sin n\theta$ in terms of powers of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ and also powers of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ in terms of multiple angles. Students should be able to prove De Moivre's theorem for any integer $n$.

kcs.title: Loci and regions in Argand diagram
kcs.statement: Loci and regions in the Argand diagram.
kcs.raw: Loci and regions in the Argand diagram.
kcs.guidance: Loci such as $|z-a| = b$, $|z-a| = k|z-b|$, $\arg(z-a) = \beta$, $\arg\left(\dfrac{z-a}{z-b}\right) = \beta$, and regions such as $|z-a| \leqslant |z-b|$ and $|z-a| \leqslant b$.

kcs.title: Transformations from z-plane to w-plane
kcs.statement: Elementary transformations from the $z$-plane to the $w$-plane.
kcs.raw: Elementary transformations from the z-plane to the w-plane.
kcs.guidance: Transformations such as $w = z^2$ and $w = \dfrac{az+b}{cz+d}$, where $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{C}$, may be set.

kcs.title: Separable first order differential equations
kcs.statement: Further solution of first order differential equations with separable variables.
kcs.raw: Further solution of first order differential equations with separable variables.
kcs.guidance: The formation of the differential equation may be required. Students will be expected to obtain particular solutions and also sketch members of the family of solution curves.

kcs.title: Linear first order differential equations
kcs.statement: First order linear differential equations of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$ where $P$ and $Q$ are functions of $x$.
kcs.raw: First order linear differential equations of the form d y x + Py = Q d where P and Q are functions of x.
glossary: e to the integral of p dx
kcs.guidance: The integrating factor $e^{\int P \, dx}$ may be quoted without proof.

kcs.title: Differential equations reducible by substitution
kcs.statement: Differential equations reducible to the above types by means of a given substitution.
kcs.raw: Differential equations reducible to the above types by means of a given substitution.

kcs.title: Second order linear differential equations
kcs.statement: The linear second order differential equation $a\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + b\dfrac{dy}{dx} + cy = f(x)$ where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are real constants and the particular integral can be found by inspection or trial.
kcs.raw: The linear second order differential x + b d y 2 y d equation a x + cy  = f(x) d 2 d where a, b and c are real constants and the particular integral can be found by inspection or trial.
kcs.guidance: The auxiliary equation may have real distinct, equal or complex roots. $f(x)$ will have one of the forms $ke^{px}$, $A + Bx$, $p + qx + cx^2$ or $m\cos\omega x + n\sin\omega x$. Students should be familiar with the terms 'complementary function' and 'particular integral'. Students should be able to solve equations of the form $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 4y = \sin 2x$.

kcs.title: Second order DEs reducible by substitution
kcs.statement: Differential equations reducible to the above types by means of a given substitution.
kcs.raw: Differential equations reducible to the above types by means of a given substitution.

kcs.title: Maclaurin series derivation and use
kcs.statement: Derivation and use of Maclaurin series.
kcs.raw: Derivation and use of Maclaurin series.
kcs.guidance: The derivation of the series expansion of $e^x$, $\sin x$, $\cos x$, $\ln(1+x)$ and other simple functions may be required.

kcs.title: Taylor series derivation and use
kcs.statement: Derivation and use of Taylor series.
kcs.raw: Derivation and use of Taylor series.
kcs.guidance: The derivation, for example, of the expansion of $\sin x$ in ascending powers of $(x - \pi)$ up to and including the term in $(x-\pi)^3$.

kcs.title: Series solutions of differential equations
kcs.statement: Use of Taylor series method for series solutions of differential equations.
kcs.raw: Use of Taylor series method for series solutions of differential equations.
kcs.guidance: Students may, for example, be required to find the solution in powers of $x$ as far as the term in $x^4$, of the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0$, such that $y = 1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$ at $x = 0$.

kcs.title: Polar coordinates and curve sketching
kcs.guidance: The sketching of curves such as $\theta = \alpha$, $r = p\sec(\alpha - \theta)$, $r = a$, $r = 2a\cos\theta$, $r = k\theta$, $r = a(1 \pm \cos\theta)$, $r = a(3 + 2\cos\theta)$, $r = a\cos 2\theta$ and $r^2 = a^2\cos 2\theta$ may be set.

kcs.title: Area enclosed by a polar curve
kcs.statement: Use of the formula $\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int_{\alpha}^{\beta} r^2 \, d\theta$ for area.
kcs.raw: β ∫ Use of the formula r 2 d θ 1 2 α for area.
kcs.guidance: The ability to find tangents parallel to, or at right angles to, the initial line is expected.
